title: modernize-scheduler-backpressure-probe-and-upgrade-deps
creator: Ava Martinez
description:
Problem: The current scheduler backpressure probe is implemented with a blocking poller that occasionally stalls under heavy ingress and exacerbates kv-cache eviction storms. Multiple production incidents in the last six months traced to transient scheduler stalls; telemetry indicates a mix of syscall blocking and sync-primitive contention. Additionally, our runtime uses older versions of tokio/jemalloc which miss latency improvements and allocator tuning shipped in upstream releases.

Goal: Replace the blocking poller with an async/await based probe, standardize a deterministic slot allocation heuristic, and upgrade critical runtime dependencies (tokio, jemalloc, parking_lot) to reduce tail latency and kv-cache churn. This ticket covers the refactor, unit/integration tests, benchmark harness updates, and a staged rollout plan with canary metrics and rollback gates.
acceptance_criteria:
- Backpressure probe replaced with async implementation with no regression in max-p99 scheduling latency (<= 5% regression allowed)
- Deterministic slot allocator introduced behind a feature flag and validated on canary; no increase in request timeouts
- tokio upgraded to 1.30.x (or latest compatible), jemalloc tuned and packaged; all builds pass CI
- KV cache eviction rate on canary reduces or remains stable compared to baseline (target: -10% eviction rate)
- Detailed performance report and playbook for rollback included in PR description
- End-to-end tests covering slot handoff, prefetch/persist interactions, and graceful shutdown pass
implementation_plan:
1) Prototype async probe in a branch with feature flag `async-backpressure-probe`. Keep existing blocking probe as default.
2) Implement deterministic slot allocator (configurable policy) and integrate with probe feedback loops.
3) Upgrade tokio -> 1.30.x and parking_lot -> latest compatible; run local CI and perf harness.
4) Upgrade jemalloc and add allocator tuning knobs; validate memory footprint under synthetic workloads.
5) Add microbenchmarks (p99/p999 scheduling latency, batch formation rates, kv-cache eviction traces).
6) Run internal canary: single-region canary with 5% traffic for 24h; monitor: scheduler-p99, kv-evictions/min, host-RSS, syscall-blocker traces.
7) Gradual rollout with automated rollback on breach of defined SLOs.
migration_steps:
- Deploy feature-flagged build to canary pool.
- After 24h, compare metrics against baseline dashboard (console/runtime/canary).
- If stable, increase traffic to 25% for 6h, then to 50% for 2h, then full.
- Provide hotfix branch for quick reversion to blocking probe and prior allocator settings if regressions detected.
benchmarks:
- Baseline harness: 10k concurrent active sessions, token length distribution: 75% short / 25% long.
- Measure: request-p99, scheduling-latency-p99, batch-size-mean, kv-evictions/min, memory-RSS.
- Target improvements: scheduling p99 -10% (or within 5% regression at worst), evictions -10%.
risks:
- Upgrading tokio may expose subtle timing changes affecting existing concurrency invariants.
- Jemalloc tuning could change memory footprint leading to OOM in older instance types.
- Deterministic allocator might reduce opportunistic locality which could transiently increase batch variance.
- Rollout must be carefully gated to avoid cross-region cascades.
notes:
- Conversation summary: runtime team review on 2026-02-12 recommended async probe + feature flag and thorough perf gates.
- QA will run synthetic degraded-network tests to ensure backpressure signal remains stable.
- Assign a safety lead to own rollback (recommended: Sophie Patel).
